perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- Keith works with Elizabeth at a construction company; he is a construction worker and she is the receptionist. Their relationship has been friendly but professional through office interactions.
- Recently, Keith observed that Elizabeth had been unusually curt/short with him for several days. He believed she might be upset with him, possibly because of a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- Keith asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and she apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and wanted to support her. He offered to listen and suggested a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted, saying that was kind and sounded good.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses; Keith perceived them as quite severe. He suggested she consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can help. Elizabeth replied that she had thought about it but was hesitant.
- Afterward, Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He regretted possibly overstepping or embarrassing her, and apologized, saying he only wanted her to know he was there to support her. Elizabeth said he didn’t overstep, appreciated his concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He told her he was glad they talked and that he is always available if she needs to chat or take a break. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship.

He does not know anything beyond what he directly observed, heard, or was told by Elizabeth.
